For home defense I concur with the Ruger 556, good bang for the buck I've never had a Ruger I didn't love, good quality control there and all American (compared to others these days). If not that, then build your own I'd say. The only thing about the Ruger is its gas-system. Its a more durable and cleaner system that uses a rod to cycle the bolt instead of the "direct gas impingement" the original AR's use, which is dirty as hell (carbon) inside the gun, but more reliable in the dirt and mud (The Ruger is superior in a clean environment though, like inside your house). Also you want to spend as much or more on the optics for it, good sights/lights/lasers are worth it. So you want to stay under $1,000 for the rifle itself.

After recording SO many names in a log book for the ATF to look up later, I'm a Yuge fan of "Ghost-guns" aka self-built guns from "80% lower receivers". Basically you get an unfinished receiver with the mag-well still filled in with metal/plastic and you drill out the remaining bit so you can order it online without an FFL (like Wal-Mart) involved. You get a completely custom gun with the parts you pick out (will take some research to know what you want) and the upper receiver can be ordered assembled with no FFL. With enough skill this is by far the best option for the money, and also the cheapest way to get a hold of a basic AR platform. You get the added bonus of nosy governments staying out of your business, (no serial numbers) AND you get exactly the rifle you want at the lowest price point possible, win/win.

It's not just AR's you can get in 80% form either. You can now get a Glock clone (any caliber), there's a 1911 (classic US WW2 pistol) and even some unique guns are offered this way from the manufacturer.

The only other thing is you have to get good with it, so budget in ammo and practice time as well. Hope that helps.
